text:
customer-jane: Hey team — since ~10:13 UTC we're seeing a spike in 5xxs and high p95 latency for EU users. A few requests were billed as cross-region egress. Example request IDs: r-82347, r-82352. Incoming header was X-Region: eu-west-1 but responses show x-served-region: us-west-2 and auth fails intermittently. CC @support-engineer

support-engineer: Thanks @customer-jane — can you paste the raw curl + response headers and any repro steps?

customer-jane: Sure, here's one verbatim (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=rwd-3"
* Connected to api.redwood.example (35.XX.XX.XX) port 443 (#0)
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< x-served-region: us-west-2
< x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 851
< content-type: application/json
{"error":"service_unavailable","request_id":"r-82347"}
```

support-engineer: Got it. I'm seeing corresponding gateway traces showing the request routed to gen-us-west-2 cluster and the upstream returned 503/401 depending on token. Escalating to SRE to check route selection.

jamal: I pulled the gateway trace for r-82347 — Envoy L7 chose cluster 'gen-us-west-2' because metadata_match fell back. The route config includes metadata_match on "region_hint" and there's a fallback policy that should *not* copy client X-Region into the fallback override, but it is doing that. Repro steps below.

jamal: Repro (staging):
```
# reproduce locally (staging)
curl -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://staging-gw.redwood/v/healthcheck?model=rwd-3 -I
# simulate eu backend down
kubectl scale deployment redwood-gen-eu --replicas=0 -n prod
curl -v -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://staging-gw.redwood/v1/generate?model=rwd-3
# observe x-served-region: us-west-2 even though X-Region was eu-west-1
```

alex: This matches a canary we rolled yesterday. We introduced a change 'route_fallback_preserve_headers' to preserve client hint headers for telemetry, but the implementation accidentally rewrites X-Region with the fallback cluster's tag during route selection. The header rewrite happens in the envoy filter when applying fallback metadata. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4321 — staging tests didn't cover the header-copy edge-case.

maria: FYI finance — cross-region egress for acct-998 spiked around 10:12-10:18 UTC. Please collect request_ids/time windows for dispute. r-82347 and r-82352 are on the list.

support-engineer: Action items: (1) SRE rollback canary change on edge (jamal) (2) Add integration test for header-preserve vs region-fallback (alex) (3) Support to collect affected request_ids and timestamps for finance (me) (4) Apply temporary edge rule to force X-Force-Region from client X-Region when available.

ops: Temporary mitigation applied: edge rule injected X-Force-Region from client's X-Region for /v1/* routes. Monitoring shows EU p95 latency dropped back to normal and 5xxs reduced. Will revert after fix.

customer-jane: Confirming latency improved and 5xxs reduced for our EU traffic. Thanks — please advise on billing remediation and final root cause.

jamal: Rolled back the canary on edge and promoted the fix to prod at 2025-09-14T11:10:03Z. We'll compile a short postmortem with timeline and traces.

alex: Follow-up created: https://git.redwood/issues/789 — add e2e test, whitelist header list so only allowed headers are preserved, and tighten route-metadata semantics. I'll open the PR to remove header-copy in the envoy transform. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deployment redwood-edge-canary reverted by jamal at 2025-09-14T11:09:58Z — status: success.

support-engineer: I'll gather the full list of affected request_ids and send to finance. Notifying @customer-jane when we have the billing info. Thanks everyone for the quick triage :clap:
